paper_title: What Does Neuro Mean to Cardio Investigating the Role of Clinical   Specialty Data in Medical LLMs
caption: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline Mistral-v0.2 and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. Each group represents tokens categorized into different clinical specialties. Each color means that the same model is further fine-tuned on each specialty data.

model_annotations.English: This bar chart illustrates the negative log probability for clinically relevant tokens between a baseline model (Mistral v0.2) and the same model further fine-tuned on data from six different clinical specialties. The horizontal axis displays “Per-specialty terms” with categories for Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics, listed in that order. The vertical axis, labeled “Negative log probability,” uses a linear scale ranging from -22 to -27, with tick marks at integer intervals. Each specialty category contains a group of bars, one for each fine-tuning dataset; the bars for Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics are all colored orange, while the bars for Neuro are light blue. Within each group, bars vary in height, with the shortest bars ranging around -22 (for Cardio and Gastro fine-tuning) and the tallest bars extending to approximately -25 (for Neuro fine-tuning). Across the groups, the bars do not appear to be sorted by height, and no bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, outlines, or annotations.
model_annotations.German: This bar chart illustrates negative log probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between a baseline model, Mistral-v0.2, and the same model fine-tuned on different specialty data. The horizontal axis represents per-specialty terms, with categories labeled “Cardio,” “Gastro,” “Infect,” “Neuro,” “Obstetrics,” and “Pediatrics,” arranged alphabetically. The vertical axis is labeled “Negative log probability” and displays a logarithmic scale ranging from -22 to -27, with tick marks at intervals of 1. For each specialty category, there are multiple bars representing the negative log probability for the corresponding model fine-tuning; these bars are colored light blue, orange, dark orange, brown, and dark brown, corresponding to fine-tuning on “Cardio,” “Gastro,” “Infect,” “Neuro,” “Obstetrics,” and “Pediatrics” respectively. Within each specialty category, the bars vary in length, representing different negative log probability values; for example, in the “Cardio” category, the light blue bar extends to approximately -22.5, while the brown bar extends to approximately -25.5. The bars are grouped by specialty, with each color within a group indicating a different fine-tuning setting. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, outlining, or annotation.
